Combining theoretical rigor with engineering practicality, the proposed model offers a reliable tool for accurate well design and production analysis in the oil and gas industry.

papers.title: Numerical study on the influence of chemical kinetic models on high-speed non-equilibrium flow and radiative characteristics
papers.abstract: Hypersonic vehicles bear more pronounced aerothermal effects due to the increase in flight altitudes and speed, underscoring the need for accurate chemical kinetic models that reflect realistic physicochemical processes to reliably predict complex flow fields, surface heat, and radiation properties. In this study, a simplified air chemistry model, self-consistently derived from a collisional-radiative model, is applied for the first time to multi-dimensional hypersonic flow simulations. Our model results show good agreement with ground experimental data for shock standoff distance and flight data on wall heat flux. Meanwhile, a comparative analysis is conducted to study the influence of different chemical models on the non-equilibrium characteristics, surface heating, and radiative properties of spherical nose models with varying radii. The results indicate that non-equilibrium effects are most pronounced at a smaller radius. Our model predicts the highest post-shock temperature, lower ionization levels, and notable differences in species composition compared to the Park, Gupta, and Dunn-Kang models. The thermochemical non-equilibrium effect significantly affects radiation mechanisms and spectral characteristics. Our model results suggest that radiation in the shock layer is dominated by molecular band emissions in the ultraviolet (UV) and vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) ranges for a flow with a Mach number of 20 at an altitude of 40 km. The radiation intensity differs considerably from that of other chemical models, highlighting that an appropriate choice of chemical reaction model is crucial for predicting non-equilibrium flow fields and radiation characteristics.

papers.title: Flow field coupling between turbine and ramjet channels during turbine-based combined cycle inlet mode transition
papers.abstract: This study investigates the flow field behavior during the mode transition of a turbine-based combined cycle (TBCC) inlet, focusing on the coupling dynamics between turbine and ramjet channels under backpressure conditions. It reveals the dual-channel interaction mechanism and identifies three distinct coupling phenomena: when both channels are started, they operate independently; when the ramjet channel is unstarted, it has no effect on the upstream flow or turbine channel; when the turbine channel is unstarted, it alters the flow structure of the ramjet channel. This study also examines flow evolution and performance parameter changes during both forward and reverse transitions. Under throttled ramjet conditions, two distinct flow behaviors emerge depending on the initial state. In forward transitions, when the inlet is starting, hysteresis occurs in the ramjet's shock train movement, and the performance trends of the turbine and ramjet channels exhibit strong symmetry. However, when the ramjet channel fails to start, the inert flow field cannot return to its original state, and this symmetry is lost.

papers.title: Aggregated self-propelled particles in microchannel-cavity structures
papers.abstract: Collective motion of self-propelled particles can utilize their own energy to achieve non-equilibrium motion, exhibiting rich swimming behaviors and particle aggregation phenomena. This study numerically investigates the regulatory mechanisms of self-propelled type parameter (β), particle number (Num) on the capture efficiency, and aggregation coefficient of self-propelled particles within microchannel-cavity structures. The study shows that by increasing the value of |β|, the capture efficiency of self-propelled particles is decreased. By increasing the value of Num, the self-propelled particles with large |β| can be effectively captured, while the particles with small |β| have limited enhancement on capture efficiency. The pullers and pushers are more likely to adhere to the left wall corner and the right wall, respectively. The low pressure and high pressure areas in the left corner and right corner formed by the contraction and expansion structure of microchannel cavity, as well as the pressure distribution near the surface of the pusher and puller, are the main reasons for particle aggregation in different positions of the cavity. This research clarifies the collective motion of self-propelled particles under complex fluid environments.

papers.title: Non-isothermal phase-field model of molten pool dynamics coupled with thermocapillary effect and phase change in metal additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: High-fidelity phase-field model (PFM) for molten pool dynamics in metal additive manufacturing (MAM) is highly required, which fully takes into account the coupled multi-physics problems of molten pool flows. Herein, we present a thermodynamically consistent non-isothermal PFM for incompressible multiphase flows with thermocapillary effects and phase change. The model is derived from a thermodynamic framework of incompressible two-phase flows, invoking the microforce theory and Coleman–Noll procedure. Features of molten pool flows, such as the large liquid–gas density ratio and temperature gradient, are fully taken into account. The model is further extended to the complicated thermo-solid–liquid–gas flows with laser-induced phase change (melting, solidification, and evaporation). Within the phase-field framework, we derive the smooth function for describing surface tension and recoil pressure acting on the molten pool and establish the thermodynamics of mass and energy losses due to evaporation. Several numerical benchmarks, such as flat gas–liquid interface, single bubble and droplet, and molten plate and particle, are introduced to validate the developed non-isothermal phase-field model. Simulation results show that the area of solidified single track is approximatively linear with the linear energy density. The non-isothermal PFM shows its ability to investigate the molten pool dynamics and pore defect formation during MAM process.

papers.title: Propulsion of microspheres by photothermally triggered cavitation bubbles at solid–liquid interfaces
papers.abstract: Cavitation bubbles, characterized by their transient and high-energy dynamics, hold great potential for microscale manipulation and propulsion. This study investigates the motion of SiO2 microspheres driven by cavitation bubbles at solid–liquid interfaces using high-speed imaging and particle image velocimetry. By tuning the cavitation bubble size, microsphere radius, and initial bubble–microsphere distance, controllable unidirectional and reciprocating motions were achieved. Two distinct interaction modes—contact and non-contact—were identified and characterized by the dimensionless parameters δ and ξ. In the contact mode, the cavitation bubble directly interacts with the microsphere, producing stronger propulsion with larger displacements and higher velocities. In contrast, in the non-contact mode, the microsphere is indirectly driven by the fluid motion induced by cavitation bubble dynamics. A force-balance model and numerical simulations further elucidated the underlying mechanisms, revealing that liquid inertia dominates the non-contact mode, whereas asymmetric pressure fields generated during the early bubble growth stage govern the contact mode. This work provides a unified understanding of cavitation-bubble-driven microsphere propulsion, offering insights for controllable micromanipulation and noncontact particle removal.

papers.title: Suppression of array resonance by biofouling-induced dissipation in wave interaction with concentric monopile-cage structures
papers.abstract: The structural integration of aquaculture facilities within offshore wind farms introduces a critical risk of collective hydrodynamic resonance, a phenomenon capable of causing catastrophic load amplifications in multi-body arrays. To address these, the present study develops a semi-analytical model, leveraging the eigenfunction expansion method and Graf's addition theorem, to analyze the wave-induced response of an Array of Concentric Monopile-Cage Integrated Structures (ACMCIS). A comprehensive parametric study uncovers a fundamental competition between wave energy amplification through collective resonance and its suppression via porosity-induced dissipation. The results demonstrate that specific array spacings can trigger powerful collective resonances, leading to hydrodynamic loads that dramatically exceed the single-body baseline. Counter-intuitively, a paradoxical dual role of biofouling is revealed: while fouling increases the direct wave load on the cages, it simultaneously acts as a powerful system-wide damper, effectively mitigating these severe resonant amplifications. Furthermore, the annular gap within each unit is identified as a critical “tuning knob” that modulates this resonant behavior. The developed model and the physical insights obtained offer a theoretical foundation essential for the safe and resilient design of these emerging multi-use platforms.

papers.title: Investigation of the run-up characteristics of landslide-generated impulse waves on the dam under the influence of the bend
papers.abstract: Landslide-generated impulse waves (LGIWs) occurring in mountain reservoirs exhibit obvious topography-related characteristics during long-term evolution. This paper conducts a comprehensive study on the run-up characteristics of impulse waves on the dam built downstream of the river bend. Large-scale physical similarity model experiments are carried out based on the potential LGIWs hazards in the Rumei (RM) reservoir to investigate the run-up process of impulse waves on the dam. Numerical simulations are then conducted using a hybrid discrete element method–smoothed particle hydrodynamics and shallow water equations model to further analyze the LGIWs disaster and the run-up evolution of impulse waves. The reasons for the complex run-up characteristics are analyzed, the influence of bends under different dam surface inclinations, and the dam position is also discussed. The results show that under the influence of the bend, the run-up process exhibits distinct temporal and spatial effects. Three wave motion patterns gradually appear at the dam surface due to the influence of the bend in front of the dam: reflected waves between the flanks, incident waves from the river, and water rebound under gravity. The maximum run-up height occurs when various factors are superimposed simultaneously, which may cause even a small incident wave to generate a large run-up height. As the inclination of the dam surface decreases, the influence of the bend on the run-up process gradually diminishes. Under the effect of the bend, the disaster of LGIWs may be amplified. This study recommends that the whole lifecycle of the LGIWs should be studied based on high-resolution terrain to get a more accurate assessment of the LGIWs disaster.

papers.title: Investigation of the bubble dynamics between two parallel plates within confined spaces
papers.abstract: The present paper investigates the bubble dynamics between two parallel plates within the confined spaces. Based on the high-speed photography experiments, the bubble typical collapse morphologies and splitting phenomena are observed under the constraint of the parallel plates. The influence of the plate spacing on the bubble centroid movements and collapse jets are quantitatively analyzed. Based on the Kelvin impulse theoretical model, flow velocity and Kelvin impulse distributions during the bubble oscillation process are investigated and compared with the experimental results. The conclusions are given as follows: (1) Three bubble splitting phenomena are identified at symmetric positions between two parallel plates: vertical split, radial expansion, and horizontal split. The difference in the transverse and longitudinal contraction velocities of the bubble interface leads to the different splitting phenomena. (2) Four collapse morphologies are identified at asymmetric positions: semi-cylindrical, triangle-shaped, bulb-shaped, and ellipse-shaped collapses. (3) As the bubble moves away from the symmetric position, its jet velocity continues to increase, and the bubble centroid displacement first increases and then decreases.

papers.title: Marine fouling roughness effects on pump-jet hydrodynamics and flow noise
papers.abstract: Marine hydraulic machinery is highly susceptible to biofouling, which alters surface roughness and degrades both hydrodynamic and acoustic performance during long-term operation. Using barnacles as representative fouling organisms, this study systematically examines the effects of fouling size and spatial distribution on pump-jet propulsion through high-fidelity numerical simulations. The flow field is resolved using the improved delayed detached eddy simulation (IDDES) turbulence model, and flow-induced noise is predicted via Lighthill's acoustic analogy. Variations in barnacle coverage and attachment locations are evaluated in terms of thrust, torque, wake characteristics, and acoustic radiation. Results show that barnacle-induced roughness disrupts boundary-layer development, intensifies turbulence, and promotes flow separation, leading to measurable performance deterioration. Under severe fouling (Type B2), the propulsion efficiency decreases by up to 29.6%, while the overall sound pressure level increases by 16.35 dB. Even mild fouling produces notable degradation, with efficiency losses of 3%–8% and a noise increase exceeding 10 dB. Larger barnacles and irregular distributions further amplify wake vortex strength and broaden low-frequency noise components, particularly at blade-passing harmonics. These findings quantify the combined hydrodynamic and acoustic penalties caused by marine biofouling and provide a theoretical basis for antifouling design, performance prediction, and maintenance planning in marine propulsion systems.

papers.title: Calibration refinement for light field particle image velocimetry through iterative polynomial model tweaking
papers.abstract: Volumetric calibration for light field particle image velocimetry (LF-PIV) establishes the voxel-to-pixel mapping and is essential for reliable particle field reconstruction. Conventional target-based calibration often degrades due to feature-localization errors and traverse uncertainties. We introduce an iterative polynomial model tweaking (IPT) strategy that improves accuracy, robustness, and generalization. A baseline polynomial model is built from calibrated-target features, and sparse flow tracers act as geometric anchors to refine the model under a regularized Levenberg–Marquardt scheme. View bias from LF sub-aperture images is explicitly modeled and compensated to decouple view-dependent offsets from geometric terms. Model stability is improved by expanding a high-confidence core to the full volume to capture higher-order aberrations. Comparative evaluations are performed against the baseline and a representative learning-based model (BP-NN) using synthetic data, and swirl flame flow experiments are conducted on a centrally staged combustor. Results indicate that IPT yields lower re-projection error than the baseline and BP-NN models and produces fewer lost and ghost particles in particle reconstructions. These gains become significant under perturbations to calibrated-target features and traverse distance. In swirl flow measurements, LF-PIV with IPT calibration achieves better agreement with benchmark planar PIV than the baseline calibration, characterized by a reduction in inlet-velocity overestimation and a smaller outward transverse bias.

papers.title: Effects of temperature stratification on the propagation of detonation wave
papers.abstract: Non-uniform fuel distribution in a rotating detonation engine (RDE) combustor is generally considered to induce local deflagration combustion, leading to the temperature stratification of the combustible mixture ahead of the detonation wave. To thoroughly investigate the propagation mechanism, the propagation processes of the detonation wave under the condition of temperature stratification are extracted and numerically performed. Through the process of decoupling and re-initiation induced by the inert gas layer, a quantitative analysis was conducted on the effects of temperature gradient and stratification ratio on the propagation process. The results demonstrate that the propagation process with an inert gas layer can be categorized into stable propagation, detonation attenuation entering the layer, re-initiation penetrating the layer, overdriven, and re-stabilization phases. The detonation wave within the high-temperature layer propagates ahead under temperature-stratified conditions. The pressure disturbance generated by expansion gives rise to a localized high-pressure zone, facilitating re-initiation and significantly reducing the re-initiation distance. The re-initiation distance decreases substantially with the increase of temperature gradient and stratification ratio. Furthermore, it is found that excessively wide inert gas layer diminishes the enhancing effect of stratification conditions on re-initiation. This finding provides valuable insights for the propagation mechanisms of detonation waves in the actual RDE combustor over complex thermodynamic conditions.

papers.title: Plasma kinetics: Anomalous transport process in a hollow cathode plume
papers.abstract: In this work, the direct kinetic method is employed to investigate the anomalous transport process of current-driven instability in the hollow cathode plume. The influences of electron Mach number, gas species, and gas flow rate on the evolution of both the electron/ion velocity distribution functions and the corresponding macroscopic quantities (bulk velocity and temperature) are carefully examined. The spatial distribution of neutral particles is determined under a conical diffusion assumption, and the role of electron–neutral classical collisions in the anomalous transport process is quantitatively evaluated. The results reveal that: (i) increasing the electron Mach number enhances particle–wave interactions, thereby accelerating the formation of electron holes, high-energy ion tails, and stronger macroscopic oscillations; (ii) lighter gas species intensify particle–wave coupling, leading to a faster and stronger non-equilibrium evolution of both electrons and ions; and (iii) a higher gas flow rate suppresses nonlinear evolution by strengthening electron–neutral classical collisions, which stabilizes the velocity distributions and reduces anomalous energy transfer from electrons to ions. These findings provide new theoretical insight into the particle–wave anomalous transport mechanism and offer valuable guidance for the design and optimization of high-performance hollow cathodes.

papers.title: Aerodynamic effects of laminar separation bubble on wind turbine iced airfoil during accretion
papers.abstract: Ice accretion on aerodynamic surfaces is associated with different profiles depending on the atmospheric and meteorological parameters. In this research, the aerodynamic effects of the laminar separation bubble region on the wind turbine cross section with DU93W210 airfoil have been studied. Four iced profiles under unsteady wind shear conditions at the nominal speed of the wind turbine have been introduced as an initial assumption. Computational fluid dynamics analyses have been performed using the finite volume discretization and turbulence calculations using the Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes equations, with solving the stress term using the shear stress transport of k–ω method. The results have been investigated by comparing the separation and reattachment points and the separation bubble length of the airfoil pressure side and suction side areas at different angles of attack. The separation bubble region remains shorter than 25% of the clean airfoil chord across various ice accretion time steps and flow angles of attack. Additionally, the rate of change in the pressure center location increases more significantly with rising angles of attack than with ice accretion duration. Iced airfoils significantly reduced aerodynamic efficiency, mainly due to lower lift and higher drag. At an angle of attack of 6°, efficiency dropped by 76.2% compared to a clean profile, showing how ice buildup severely impacts performance over time.

papers.title: Effect mechanism of dielectric barrier discharge plasma excitation layouts on vortex-induced pressure oscillations in solid rocket motors
papers.abstract: Vortex-induced pressure oscillations in the combustion chambers of solid rocket motors represent a critical challenge to their reliability, and traditional passive control methods struggle to actively regulate the flow instability process. Taking a current experimental motor, C1x, as a reference, this paper employs a numerical methodology that couples large eddy simulation with a dielectric barrier discharge plasma model to systematically investigate the suppression mechanism of plasma excitations on vortex-induced pressure oscillations. The results show that the effect of plasma excitations on pressure suppression does not exhibit a linear superposition relationship with increasing axial number. Under the condition that the plasma excitation intensity is set to 15, the double-row axial arrangement reduces the relative amplitude of pressure oscillations at the main frequency from 0.08% (single-row) to 0.030%. This demonstrates that the suppression effect of the double-row plasma arrangement is significantly superior to that of the single-row arrangement overall. The number of circumferential plasma excitations has no significant effect on suppressing pressure oscillations in the motor. The closer the excitation position is to the backward-facing step where the vortex is generated, the more strongly the induced vortices there are broken, enhancing the suppression of pressure oscillations. A plasma excitation located at twice the boundary layer thickness upstream from the step achieves optimal pressure oscillation suppression. Compared with an incidence direction parallel to the mainstream, vertical and opposite-direction plasma incidence yields a higher vortex rotation intensity and better suppression, which can reduce the maximum relative amplitude of pressure oscillations from 0.07% to 0.027%.

papers.title: Direct numerical simulations of activation and deactivation in turbulent atmospheric clouds
papers.abstract: Significant knowledge gaps remain in our understanding of turbulence–cloud–aerosol interactions in the Earth's atmosphere, and direct numerical simulation (DNS) has increasingly become an indispensable tool to fill such critical knowledge gaps. This study is an extension of our previous DNS model [Gao et al., J. Geophys. Res.: Atmos., 123(4), 2194–2214 (2018)], with a focus on the activation of aerosol particles into cloud droplets and deactivation of cloud droplets into aerosol particles in a microscale cloud environment. The effects of turbulence intensity, particle curvature, and solute, as well as the initial distributions of the aerosol particles (monodisperse or polydisperse) are investigated. The governing equations for the flow of air, temperature, and water vapor mixing ratio are solved numerically in the Eulerian fashion, assuming homogeneous and isotropic turbulence. The dynamics of the aerosol and cloud particles are calculated with the Lagrangian particle tracking method. The results show that the deviations of the thermodynamic variables from their respective means are significantly reduced, the activation process appears to be delayed, and the deactivation process occurs more rapidly, as the turbulence intensity is increased. The inclusion of particle curvature and solute effects, as well as polydispersity, tends to retard the activation of aerosols into cloud droplets. It is also observed that fluctuations in supersaturation broaden the spread of particle radii, and the broadening is followed by a narrowing as turbulent homogenization reduces thermodynamic fluctuations over time.

papers.title: Numerical simulation of column separation in pipelines by discrete vapor cavity model with gas release
papers.abstract: Water hammer with column separation is a highly dangerous phenomenon in long-distance water transmission pipelines, potentially leading to structural damage or even loss of life. During the transient process, when pressure drops below the saturation pressure of dissolved gases, dissolved gases are released. However, the classical discrete vapor cavity model (DVCM) does not fully account for this effect, causing deviations in predicting the pressure peak and phase. This study innovatively incorporates a variable-mass gas release model into the DVCM, establishing the discrete vapor cavity model with gas release (DVCM-GR). Sensitivity analyses on grid resolution, weighting factors, and semi-empirical gas release rate coefficients were conducted, with results compared to both classic DVCM and experimental data. The results indicate that the prediction of pressure wave peak by the DVCM-GR model is mainly influenced by grid resolution, while the phase of the pressure wave is affected by the combined effect of all three factors. Specifically, an increase in grid resolution and semi-empirical gas release rate coefficient enhances the released gas mass, decreasing wave speed and causing phase delay, whereas a larger weighting factor produces the opposite effect. Compared with the DVCM, the DVCM-GR mitigates phase deviation and improves both peak and waveform predictions, especially when coupled with the Vardy and Brown friction model. This study highlights the significance of gas release effects in the simulation of water hammer with column separation, providing a new model option and theoretical foundation for more accurate transient analysis in pressurized pipelines.

papers.title: Experimental investigation on capillary bridge dynamics and adhesive forces in porous structures
papers.abstract: The stability and adhesion of capillary bridges are fundamental to processes in diverse fields, from pharmaceutical powder handling and food processing to microfluidics and geophysics. While critical, the evolution of these bridges under the combined influence of evaporation and mechanical traction remains poorly quantified, limiting the predictive accuracy of current models. This study presents an experimental investigation into the complex dynamics of capillary bridges formed between two spherical surfaces under these coupled conditions. A novel experimental facility was designed for the precise, simultaneous measurement of capillary adhesion force and the real-time tracking of the bridge's morphological evolution using water and ethanol as a working fluid. This integrated approach allows for direct correlation between mechanical forces and dynamic geometric changes. Using high-speed imaging and advanced image processing, key geometric parameters, including neck radius, contact angle, and bridge height, were extracted from the axisymmetric bridges. The results reveal that the substrate surface characteristics significantly influence the adhesive force, leading to distinct and predictable behaviors for water vs ethanol. The data empirically validate key theoretical predictions, quantifying the dependence of adhesion force on bridge volume and the inverse relationship with bridge height. Furthermore, fluctuations in Laplace pressure and contact angles were directly linked to transient, evaporation-driven mass loss and traction-induced changes in curvature. These findings offer crucial new insights into the role of fluid–substrate interactions in capillary-mediated adhesion. The comprehensive dataset and analysis provide a robust foundation for refining mechanistic models used to simulate and control particulate systems where capillary forces are dominant.

papers.title: Computational modeling of squeezed blood flow in deformable veins: Application to calf muscle pump during walking
papers.abstract: This study introduces a three-dimensional mathematical model to simulate blood flow in the calf muscle, conceptualized as a non-Newtonian fluid within a vertical conduit experiencing a squeezing motion. The model includes hybrid nanoparticles (Ag-Fe3O4) and takes into account the effects of an external magnetic field, such as the Hall current effect, and an external heating source. The governing system, based on the basic laws of conservation of mass, momentum, energy, and nanoparticle concentration, is made up of a group of partial differential equations that are linked together. A similarity transformation technique turns these equations into a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations. The Optimal Homotopy Asymptotic Method (OHAM) is used to analytically solve the resulting system. The analysis examines essential physiological parameters such as pressure, velocity components, temperature, and nanoparticle concentration to clarify their behavior under the influence of combined physical effects. The graphical and tabular results show that the hybrid nanoparticle case has the highest pressure profiles. This suggests that there is a synergistic effect that makes flow resistance stronger. This suggests a possible trade-off in nanoparticle-enhanced therapies; although advantageous for targeted drug delivery or diagnostic imaging, elevated concentrations may disrupt normal hemodynamics by increasing metabolic strain or compromising oxygen delivery.

papers.title: A review of cavitation dynamics in liquid rocket engine turbopump inducers
papers.abstract: Cavitation dynamics, such as cavitation surge and rotating cavitation, are natural performance limits for turbopump inducers and pose a significant risk to the development and operation of liquid rockets. In the last 63 years, progress has been made in understanding cavitation instabilities and their relationship to cavitation number, inlet flow coefficient, rotating speed, inducer size, and thermal effects. However, we are still unable to predict the cavitation behavior of a real inducer installed in rocket engines or contribute much to the design of a more cavitation-resistant machine. This paper comprehensively reviews findings from computational fluid dynamics simulations, reduced-order modeling, and experiments in cryogenic fluids and water, focusing on the effects of compressibility on multiphase flow calculations, the assessment of cavitation compliance and mass flow gain factor, and their influences on cavitation stability analysis, as well as the transfer function for cavitating inducers. This review will provide insights for future research to achieve more accurate performance predictions, improve flow modeling, and enhance the interpretation of experimental results.

papers.title: Experimental investigation of phase transition effects on impact pressure dynamics in sloshing flows
papers.abstract: The safe and efficient marine transportation of cryogenic fuels such as liquefied natural gas (LNG) presents significant technical challenges, particularly under sloshing conditions where violent impact may occur. Investigating phase transition effects in LNG sloshing is crucial for enhancing transport safety, since phase transition is an inherent feature of near-equilibrium sloshing whose effects on sloshing impacts have not been thoroughly understood. This study experimentally investigates the influence of phase transition on sloshing flow characteristics and impact loads. Utilizing a customized sloshing model tank and the refrigerant R141b, sloshing experiments are conducted under both phase transition and non-phase transition conditions. By analyzing high-speed images of the sloshing evolutions, typical sloshing modes are classified. Long-duration impact pressure signals are collected and analyzed from multiple perspectives in both time and frequency domains to characterize how phase transition modifies the evolution of impact pressure waveforms. In consideration of the randomness of pressure signals, statistical analyses of pressure peaks are also performed, revealing that phase transition leads to reduced peak values, narrower distributions, and decreased variability. Furthermore, the study explores the implications of pressure rise time on dynamic structural response. The findings provide essential insights into incorporating phase transition mechanisms into impact load assessment frameworks. This contributes to the development of safer, more reliable, and cost-effective design standards for LNG containment systems in marine transportation.

papers.title: Computational investigation of iris melanoma effects on aqueous humor dynamics in the anterior chamber of the human eye
papers.abstract: Iris melanoma, a rare but potentially vision-threatening malignancy, can significantly disrupt the physiological flow of aqueous humor (AH) within the anterior chamber (AC) of the human eye. Such disruptions may affect intraocular pressure (IOP) regulation and overall ocular fluid dynamics, leading to complications in disease progression and treatment outcomes. In this study, a computational model is developed to examine the impact of iris melanoma on AH dynamics. The tumor is represented as a solid obstruction located on the iris surface. The governing Navier–Stokes and energy equations are solved using ANSYS Fluent to simulate steady-state AH flow under physiological conditions. Key parameters, including velocity fields, IOP, wall shear stress, skin friction coefficient, strain rate, and flow patterns, are analyzed and compared with results from existing literature. The findings reveal that the presence of iris melanoma induces localized flow disturbances and increases IOP within the AC. This study provides important insights into the biomechanical consequences of iris melanoma and supports the development of improved clinical assessment and treatment planning strategies through patient-specific computational modeling.

papers.title: Asymmetric hydraulic jump prediction based on interpretable soft voting ensemble learning
papers.abstract: Against the backdrop of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, some water conservancy projects have begun adopting combined energy dissipation arrangements featuring both spillway tunnels and spillways. However, due to variations in inflow characteristics across different spillway structures, the flow distribution within stilling basin becomes non-uniform and turbulent. This paper addresses the issues of non-uniform flow distribution and turbulent flow patterns within stilling basin caused by asymmetric inflow in combined spillway tunnel and spillway channel energy dissipation arrangements. It proposes an energy dissipation scheme involving the installation of a twisted bucket lip at the spillway channel outlet to generate an asymmetric hydraulic jump. Numerical simulations yielded 140 sets of data of asymmetric hydraulic jump length, with experimental validation confirming the reliability of the simulated results. Simultaneously, multiple machine learning models were employed for length of hydraulic jump prediction. Results indicate that extreme gradient boosting, categorical gradient boosting, and light gradient boosting machine delivered optimal performance. To further enhance the prediction accuracy, this study constructed an ensemble model based on soft voting, integrating the strengths of all three approaches to improve predictive precision. The interpretability analysis revealed that the width ratio (β) exerted the strongest influence on the hydraulic jump length, while the segment ratio (α) showed a negative correlation with the length of the hydraulic jump, and the Froude number (Fr) exhibited a positive correlation. This ensemble model provides an effective tool for accurately predicting the asymmetric hydraulic jump under low Froude number conditions, demonstrating significant engineering application value.

papers.title: Characterization and performance optimization of deep-sea polymetallic nodule mining considering changes in the traveling posture of mining vehicles
papers.abstract: With the advancement of deep-sea mining technology, long-distance continuous operation and extraction represent the key technical challenges for the commercialization of deep-sea mineral resources. This paper quantifies the degree of reduction in mining performance under different mine vehicle orientations and conducts research on flow field optimization. The results indicate that when the inclination angle is ≤3°, the Coandă jet maintains a stable wall-attached flow, with the collection efficiency remaining above 70%. As the inclination angle increases to 8°–14°, the pressure-induced flow structure generated by wall adhesion progressively deteriorates. The low-pressure region significantly narrows, and collection efficiency drops below 40%. This demonstrates its high sensitivity to attitude changes. Therefore, this study proposes a flow field optimization method aimed at enlarging the effective fluid action zone. The results show that after optimizing the flow field structure, the momentum coupling within the channel is significantly enhanced, and the wall-attached flow region is expanded. Under the 3° condition, the collection efficiency increases from 20% to 98%. Based on this, a dimensionless ratio parameter k was introduced to characterize the relationship between the vehicle posture, traveling parameters, and jet operating conditions. The results show that k effectively distinguishes the collection characteristics under different working conditions: when k < 50, the collection efficiency is significantly low, whereas when k ≥ 150, the efficiency approaches saturation. Therefore, in practical engineering design, k ≥ 150 should be ensured to achieve efficient mining. This study provides both theoretical and technical support for achieving efficient collection performance of deep-sea mining equipment under complex seabed conditions.

papers.title: Suppression of Kelvin–Helmholtz instability by an electric field
papers.abstract: This study investigates the dynamics of the Kelvin–Helmholtz instability in perfectly dielectric fluids in the presence of a tangential electric field. The motion of the interface is described by a vortex sheet. We show that the interface is linearly stable for Re<2|Aϵ|, where Re denotes the ratio of the inertial force to the electric force, and Aϵ represents the Atwood number for electric permittivity. We perform numerical simulations for the interface evolution for both stable and unstable regimes. The numerical results show the stabilizing effect of the electric field on the interface evolution when the electric field is sufficiently strong. In the stable regime, a nonlinear surface wave appears and propagates along the interface. Notably, the interface is nonlinearly unstable for Re≈2|Aϵ| in the linearly stable regime. We compare the unstable evolutions of the interface for wide ranges of parameters Re and Aϵ. As Re decreases, the spiral turns are significantly weakened and the spiral core is deformed. Increasing |Aϵ| has a similar effect on the interface as decreasing Re. Reversing the sign of Aϵ makes the interface morphology symmetric with respect to the center of the initial interface.

papers.title: Water-entry hydrodynamics of a trans-media flying wing
papers.abstract: Inspired by the water-entry strategies of amphibious birds, this study introduces a bio-inspired flying wing for efficient transition from air to water. A volume-of-fluid multiphase flow model coupled with the shear stress transport k–ω turbulence model is employed to investigate the two-phase flow dynamics during water entry. The stability, hydrodynamic loads, and energy efficiency of the proposed configuration are examined by systematically varying the contraction ratio, structural density, water-entry angle, and velocity. Results show that flying wings with smaller aspect ratios and lower densities, entering water at lower velocities and larger angles, exhibit slower attitude variations and improved stability, but at the cost of higher energy loss. Furthermore, increased wing contraction and reduced entry velocity significantly mitigate the impact loads. To describe these specific relationships, we define a coupling multi-parameter impact index and a comprehensive stability metric, demonstrating a strong linear correlation. These findings advance our understanding of biological water-entry behavior and provide valuable guidance for the design of bio-inspired flying wings in trans-media vehicles.

papers.title: Water–air interactions in channel-tunnel water conveyance systems with different inflow conditions
papers.abstract: Affected by increasing water demand or extreme factors, channel-tunnel water conveyance systems face such as air-pocket entrapment and pressure fluctuations during transitions between free-surface flow to pressured flow, posing serious threats to both structural safety and water conveyance efficiency. This study analyzes the evolution of flow patterns, air-pocket transport characteristics, and the dynamic response of hydraulic parameters in tunnels under both steady and unsteady inflows. The results indicate that under steady inflow conditions, the flow regime is delineated by the dimensionless discharge Q*. Throughout the transition from free-surface flow to pressured flow, the air pressure initially rises then falls, whereas the flow velocity increases monotonically. Under unsteady inflow conditions, the tunnel filling process comprises four stages: rapid compression, slow venting, pressure oscillation, and stable recovery. The slow venting stage exhibits low air venting efficiency. The most severe pressure surges occur during the oscillation stage, with pressure fluctuation amplitudes reaching 10–25 times those under steady flow conditions. These pressure fluctuations diminish along the tunnel's length, with the upstream experiencing negative pressure, while the downstream is subject to positive pressure. Accounting for factors such as flow surge intensity and tunnel geometry, a dimensionless parameter S is proposed to characterize the water–air dynamics in tunnels. The air venting rate increases with S, though pressure oscillations are also intensified. Air-pocket migration modes and pressure oscillation levels are categorized into three S intervals: S < 0.180 (slug flow-dominated migration with weak pressure oscillations), 0.180 < S < 0.780 (alternating bubbly-slug flow migration with moderate-to-strong pressure oscillations), and S > 0.780 (rapid unidirectional air migration with strong pressure oscillations). These results serve as a guideline for the safe design and efficient operation of water conveyance tunnels.

papers.title: Starting transient spray characteristics of a twin-fluid internal-mixing ramp injector: Annular flow
papers.abstract: The atomization characteristics of a twin-fluid internal-mixing ramp injector during starting transient are experimentally investigated for the annular flow regime using high-speed shadowgraph images synchronized with pressure measurements. The present study demonstrates six phases: mist flow, mist flow with annular liquid ejection, annular liquid ejection, one-sided liquid ejection, slug expansion, and annular shearing. These phases unfold in a repeatable sequence, governed by the interplay of internal gas-liquid dynamics and external aerodynamic shear. A high-velocity droplet-laden core appears early in the starting transient, followed by progressive liquid sheet formation and circumferential shearing. Additionally, the intermittent slug expulsions result in rapid gas expansion and liquid fragmentation, which ultimately transform into a fully developed annular flow. The modal analyses on high-speed images reveal spatially coherent structures, oscillating at various dominant frequencies, which are in harmonics. It is observed that the annular flow produces fine droplets even during early transients, in contrast to bubbly and slug flows, where atomization is delayed or localized. These findings highlight the superior atomization performance of the annular flow and its potential suitability for ignition reliability in a scramjet engine.

papers.title: Breakup dynamics of continuous liquid jets under radial velocity perturbations
papers.abstract: This study investigates the breakup dynamics of continuous inkjet printing (CIJ) subjected to radial velocity disturbances. Based on energy conservation, a theoretical relationship between the jet breakup length and the amplitude of radial velocity disturbance is first derived. The influence of disturbance amplitude (ϵ0′) and wavenumber (k′) on the jet breakup characteristics is investigated through direct numerical simulations employing the volume-of-fluid (VOF) multiphase model. Numerical simulations reveal that for disturbance amplitudes in the range ϵ0′=0.001∼0.1, increasing ϵ0′ significantly reduces the breakup length, following the relation Lb′∼ ln (2/ϵ0′2). Furthermore, the disturbance wavenumber k′ is found to determine the size and spacing of the resulting droplets, following the scaling laws d/D0∼k′−1/3 and S/d∼k′−2/3, respectively. A phase diagram in the ϵ0′–k′ space is constructed to classify three distinct breakup regimes: uniform droplet formation, one-droplet merging and filament breakup with multiple satellite droplets. At the optimal wavenumber k′=0.7, the effects of the Weber number and disturbance amplitude on the pinch-off behavior are further examined, identifying three ligament pinch-off modes: backward-merging, uniform, and forward-merging modes. These findings provide theoretical guidance for droplet control and prediction in applications such as continuous inkjet, extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) technology, and microfluidics.

papers.title: A boundary integral simulation of ferrofluid droplet emulsion in shear flow: Cluster formation, deformation, and specific viscosity
papers.abstract: Recent numerical studies have focused on the deformation, breakup, and rheological behavior of single ferrofluid droplets under shear flow. However, research on ferrofluid droplet emulsions remains limited due to computational challenges involved. In this study, a fully graphics processing unit-accelerated boundary integral method framework is developed for simulating ferrofluid droplet emulsions in a triply periodic domain under simple shear flow with a uniform magnetic field. The method combines Ewald summation, multipole expansion for fast far-field evaluation, and near-field regularization to stably resolve close interactions. A magnetic field imposed perpendicular to the shear plane promotes chain-like clustering through coupled magnetic and hydrodynamic interactions. Clusters are only found in the presence of a magnetic field, but the cluster length decreases as the shear rate increases. Therefore, the balance between magnetic and hydrodynamic interactions is crucial for cluster formation. In addition, droplet deformation decreases owing to the reduced cross-sectional radius in the shear plane; rescaling, guided by the small deformation theory, organizes the data across volume fractions. The orientation trends are consistent with the deformation–orientation relation, with dense emulsions exhibiting smaller angles than dilute emulsions. The specific viscosity is reduced under the magnetic field across volume fractions, with a larger relative decrease at low flow strengths, where the clusters are most pronounced. Collectively, these findings establish a relationship among field-driven alignment, deformation control, and macroscopic rheology, suggesting practical routes to control the structure–property relationships in ferrofluid droplet emulsions.

papers.title: An open-source Euler–Lagrangian solver for two-phase detonative and supersonic reacting flows
papers.abstract: Comprehending the flame propagation in detonative and supersonic combustion is critical for enabling next-generation aerospace propulsion. To capture the underlying combustion dynamics of high-speed reactive flows, an open-source hybrid Eulerian–Lagrangian solver, dfHighSpeedFoam is developed. To verify the integrated high-order numerical schemes, a series of benchmark cases is conducted in this study. The results demonstrate the capability of dfHighSpeedFoam in accurately resolving the coupled interactions between shock waves and chemical reactions. To further assess the performance of this solver, the advanced Lagrangian models are rigorously validated across a range of operating conditions and distinct submodels are comparatively assessed across regimes. The implanted liquidEvaporationSpalding model is deemed most suitable for predicting the dynamics of fine droplets in subsonic flows, whereas the liquidEvaporationBoil model is more appropriate for supersonic conditions. In simulations of two-phase detonations, dfHighSpeedFoam effectively captures the characteristic features, including the detonation propagation speed and cell size. Furthermore, the influence of different Lagrangian submodels on two-phase cavity-stabilized supersonic combustion is investigated. The findings indicate that the application of liquidEvaporationBoil and ReitzKHRT models induces a dispersed-flame regime, underscoring a strong sensitivity of flame stabilization to submodels combination. Future extensions of this study will focus on enhancing the computational efficiency of dfHighSpeedFoam and Lagrangian models.

papers.title: Erratum: “Comparative heat transfer analysis on Fe3O4–H2O and Fe3O4–Cu–H2O flow inside a tilted square porous cavity with shape effects” [Phys. Fluids 35 , 022007 (2023)]
Erratum: “Unsteady heat transfer and entropy analysis in a cavity with different fin shapes: A numerical and multi-expression programming approach” [Phys. Fluids 37 , 073616 (2025)]
Effect of recess position on fluid resonance in a recessed moonpool
papers.abstract: This study numerically investigates the effect of recess position on internal fluid resonance in recessed moonpools using a two-dimensional multiphase viscous flow solver. This is motivated by the fact that the horizontal placement of the recess relative to the incident wave direction alters geometric asymmetry, thereby modulating nonlinear free-surface dynamics and intermodal energy coupling. A systematic analysis is conducted to clarify how recess location affects frequency- and spatial-dependent amplitude operators, as well as transient phase adjustment processes. Results indicate that the right recess promotes faster phase stabilization and more effective energy synchronization with incident waves, yielding stronger resonant oscillations. Time-resolved wavelet spectrogram and Fourier harmonic decomposition reveal that the right configuration intensifies nonlinear harmonic generation and broadens the spatial and spectral energy distribution. Spatial modal decomposition further shows enhanced excitation of higher-order sloshing modes and stronger multimodal interactions over a wider frequency range. The influence of recess position on piston-mode radiation damping is also elucidated, highlighting its impact on frequency-dependent wave reflection and transmission. Additionally, viscous energy dissipation is evaluated via vorticity field analysis. The findings of this study provide new physical insights into the geometric sensitivity of moonpool resonance and offer practical guidance for recess placement in engineering applications.

papers.title: Passive flow control in lift-type vertical-axis wind turbines using optimized flaps
papers.abstract: This study demonstrates the passive control of airflow through lift-type vertical-axis wind turbines (VAWTs) by incorporating flaps on the rear of the blades. The objective is to enhance aerodynamic performance, particularly the power coefficient, by optimizing the flap configuration to its fullest potential. We employ high-fidelity two-dimensional unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes simulations with the transition shear stress transport turbulence model to examine the impact of flap length, angle, and chordwise location on turbine performance during dynamic stall. The simulation strategy is founded on a Taguchi experimental design. A machine learning (ML) model utilizing an artificial neural network is developed on computational fluid dynamics (CFD) results to comprehend the nonlinear correlation between flap parameters and power output. This reduces the expense of performing numerous simulations. This surrogate is integrated with a covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy to efficiently identify optimal flap configurations. The integrated CFD-ML–optimization framework demonstrates that optimally designed flaps can significantly enhance the turbine's power coefficient by altering the patterns of local flow separation and vorticity. The proposed method enhances the aerodynamics of VAWTs and is both computationally efficient and conceptually clear in its physical principles. This exemplifies a surrogate-assisted optimization study centered on passive flaps in VAWTs.

papers.title: Short-term prediction of wind vector at multi-heights via deep learning techniques based on marine measurements from Light-Detection-and-Ranging device
papers.abstract: Accurate short-term forecasts of offshore wind vectors are essential for exploring wind energy in marine environment. Prior studies largely emphasize wind-speed prediction at a single height, while short-term forecasting of wind vectors at multi-heights has been insufficiently investigated. Meanwhile, despite the fast development of deep learning (DL) techniques, there is a lack of research on comparing the prediction performance of varied DL models. Using long-term LiDAR measurements over 10 altitudes (22–179 m), we benchmark 4 DL models, i.e., long short term memory (LSTM), Convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM), Transformer, and Informer, for short-term forecasts of wind vectors (i.e., speed and direction) with varied lead times. A vector-decomposition strategy is adopted to remove directional wraparound discontinuities. Results demonstrate that: for the single-height forecasting scenario, ConvLSTM and Informer yield the most accurate speed predictions (R2 = 0.996, coefficient of determination), while Informer best predicts direction (R2 = 0.916); for the scenario at multi-heights, ConvLSTM provides the most accurate and vertically stable results, reflecting its advantage in spatiotemporal feature extraction. Meanwhile, the vector-decomposition strategy is found to work well. Results also show that prediction errors tend to be larger under weak/non-stationary wind conditions, and they also grow with enlarged lead time (e.g., ConvLSTM wind-speed Root Mean Square Error increases from 0.72 m/s at 30 min to 1.25 m/s at 120 min). These results offer useful guidance on model selection: ConvLSTM for multi-height speed, Informer for direction at short leads, and both for operational forecasting under marine conditions.

papers.title: Kelvin–Helmholtz instability in binary fluids with miscibility gap
papers.abstract: The isothermal spatiotemporal evolution of an interface between binary fluids, with temperature-sensitive miscibility gap, subjected to shear flow is investigated using direct numerical simulations. The thermophysical properties and the interfacial tension in such fluids exhibit a dynamic temperature dependence based on the degree of miscibility. These fluid pairs can therefore be deployed in crucial microfluidic applications involving enhancement of liquid–liquid mass transfer. In this study, a modified phase-field approach that allows modeling of partially miscible fluids and continuous transition from an initially immiscible state to a completely miscible state is employed to investigate the Kelvin–Helmholtz (KH) instability. The analysis entails two different configurations based on the thermodynamic state of the system. In the first configuration, the fluid pair is considered in equilibrium at different degrees of partially miscibility. The results reveal the effect of apparent surface tension in miscible fluids, shear flow profile, the degree of stratification, the density ratio, and the effect of mass redistribution across the interface. The shear instability in a fluid pair close to the consolute point is found to be independent of the extent of stratification. The second configuration, on the other hand, deals with fluid pair considered at a temperature above the upper critical solution temperature, thereby leading to non-equilibrium configuration. The study reveals the existence of the diffusion-dominated regime and the advection-dominated regime in the process of the development of the KH instability. The prevalence of these regimes is found to be governed by the combination of the initial degree of partial miscibility and the corresponding initial surface tension of the binary fluid pair.

papers.title: Lattice Boltzmann method-discrete element method coupling study on the hydrodynamics of waves generated by granular collapse into water
papers.abstract: This study investigates the hydrodynamics of tsunami-like waves induced by granular column collapse into water using a coupled lattice Boltzmann-discrete element method. Three-dimensional numerical simulations were carried out to evaluate the effects of column aspect ratio, particle diameter, and water depth on wave evolution and the impact forces exerted on downstream structures. Results show that larger particles enhance wave amplitude and accelerate crest propagation by reducing internal dissipation, whereas smaller particles generate deeper cavities that recover more rapidly. Increased water depth augments hydrostatic pressure, dynamic impulse loading, and reflection velocity. Force analysis further indicates that the downstream wall is subjected to both hydrostatic and dynamic pressures, with peak forces rising by approximately 50% at larger aspect ratios, a = 2.5. Channel-bed loading is primarily controlled by gravity, with pulsations linked to collapse dynamics that diminish as equilibrium is approached. These findings enhance understanding of landslide-induced wave hydrodynamics and their potential impact on downstream defenses.

papers.title: The complex structure of electrohydrodynamic flows arising in a two-phase liquid with weakly conducting dispersion medium and unequal ions mobilities
papers.abstract: The study numerically investigates the electrohydrodynamics of conducting droplets in leaky dielectric dispersion medium under high electric fields, with focus on how electrophysical properties of the dispersion medium (ion mobility, electrical conductivity) govern droplet dynamics and their pair interactions in cases of unequal ion mobilities. Using the arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian method with sharp interface resolution, the qualitative and quantitative effects of these parameters on space charge formation, Coulomb forces, and electrohydrodynamic flows were analyzed. The results reveal that asymmetric ion transport in most cases results in rapid translational motion of droplets along the force lines of the external electric field, while strong asymmetry (mobilities differ five times) may lead to intense reverse flows in droplet traces, which under specific conductivity and mobility ranges prevent droplet collision despite dipole–dipole attraction. Dimensionless analysis reduces 11 physical parameters of the system to 7 dimensionless ones, which simplifies the prediction of emulsion dynamics. The paper contains a large amount of simulation results for various system parameters and recommendations for scaling epy problem to optimize emulsion analysis.

papers.title: Guiding diffusion models to reconstruct flow fields from sparse data
papers.abstract: The reconstruction of unsteady flow fields from limited measurements is a challenging and crucial task for many engineering applications. Machine learning models are gaining popularity for solving this problem due to their ability to learn complex patterns from data and to generalize across diverse conditions. Among these, diffusion models have emerged as being particularly powerful for generative tasks, producing high-quality samples by iteratively refining noisy inputs. In contrast to other methods, these generative models are capable of reconstructing the smallest scales of the fluid spectrum. In this work, we introduce a novel sampling method for diffusion models that enables the reconstruction of high-fidelity samples by guiding the reverse process using the available sparse data. Moreover, we enhance the reconstructions with available physics knowledge using a conflict-free update method during training. To evaluate the effectiveness of our method, we conduct experiments on 2 and 3-dimensional turbulent flow data. Our method consistently outperforms other diffusion-based methods in predicting the fluid's structure and in pixel-wise accuracy. This study underscores the remarkable potential of diffusion models in reconstructing flow field data, paving the way for leveraging them in fluid dynamics research and applications ranging from super-resolution to reconstructions of experiments.

papers.title: Piezoelectric energy harvesting in a nonlinear fluid-conveying pipe attached with quasi-zero-stiffness units
papers.abstract: Quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) mechanisms have been widely employed in engineering structures for vibration isolation. However, they also possess the potential for regulating energy harvesting performance, contributing to a multifunctional structure. Motivated by this characteristic, this study constructs a geometrically nonlinear fluid-conveying pipe outfitted with piezoelectric (PZT) layers for energy conversion and QZS units as tunable attachments. The PZT layers harvest the vibrations resulting from serving environments, and the QZS units shape the system's frequency response and place the effective harvesting band without active control. Practically, adjusting the vertical stiffness trades isolation against available motion amplitude, while the horizontal stiffness (negative-stiffness level) and the number of QZS units act as “tuning knobs” for band location. Within the fluid–structure interaction context, changes in flow velocity shift structural resonance bands, and the PZT–circuit resistance and excitation level govern the electromechanical coupling strength and output level. Such a novel design integrates low-frequency vibration isolation with tunable energy harvesting, offering both theoretical guidance and an engineering scheme for advanced fluid-conveying systems.

papers.title: Water wave–current interaction with logarithmic wind-induced current
papers.abstract: The effect of wind-induced logarithmic current shear on the wave dispersion relationship, the linear wave velocity, and the Stokes-drift velocity as a function of depth has been theoretically studied in regular deep-water wave conditions by accounting for the vorticity caused by the current. A formula showing how wind-induced current shear affects the wave dispersion relationship is derived. Case studies show that the current shear influences the wavelengths, which affect, e.g., dynamic pressure and wave velocity. In the linear analysis, the logarithmic current shear has a singularity at the mean free surface, leading to unrealistic predictions of the horizontal wave velocity and the Stokes drift velocity in a thin layer near the mean free surface. Since the wind-induced current must satisfy boundary conditions on the instantaneous free surface, strong nonlinearities occur in the predictions of the horizontal wave velocity near the free surface. The effect of current shear on the linear wave excitation loads on a pontoon of a planned floating bridge in Bjørnafjorden is assessed. An error analysis indicates that neglecting current shear introduces acceptable errors, which are comparable in magnitude to those caused by disregarding viscous flow separation around the structure.

papers.title: Rossby wave radiation on the Β-plane by western and eastern boundary currents
papers.abstract: The linear problem of Rossby wave radiation by meridional boundary currents is considered. The spectral problem is conditionally divided into two regions: the long-wavelength region (l < 0.5) and the short-wavelength region (l > 0.5) (where l is the meridional wavenumber normalized to the current width). It is shown that in the long-wavelength part of the spectrum (l < 0.5), a quasimonochromatic Rossby wave is radiated into the open ocean, and an asymmetry between the western and eastern boundary currents is observed. The western boundary current radiates Rossby waves with small growth increments. The wavenumber and group velocity of the radiated Rossby wave in the open ocean are practically zonal and oppositely directed (the phase propagates westward, the group velocity is directed eastward). The eastern current, conversely, radiates Rossby waves with large growth increments. The wavenumber is directed almost meridionally, and the group velocity is directed westward. Rossby waves radiated by the eastern current are an order of magnitude longer than waves radiated by the western current. In the short-wavelength region (l > 0.5), the radiation of Rossby waves into the open ocean disappears. The asymmetry between east and west also disappears. The solution, for both the eastern and western boundary currents, converges to a varicose Rayleigh mode and consists of a chain of small (compared to the current width) cyclones and anticyclones located on the outer boundary of the current (on the open ocean side). Verification of this model using the example of the Lofoten Basin in the Norwegian Sea has shown that typical nondimensional β values at mid-latitudes are closer to 0.01 rather than β = 0.5.

papers.title: Near-wall accumulation of inertial particles in compressible turbulent channel flows
papers.abstract: In the present study, the accumulation of inertial particles in compressible turbulent channel flow is investigated by direct numerical simulations. In particular, an investigation is conducted into how the Mach number and Stokes number affect particle transport, where Mach numbers are taken as Ma=1.5 and 3, Stokes numbers (St0+) span from 1 to 200, and the Reynolds number is fixed at Re=3000. It is found that particles tend to concentrate in the low-velocity, high-density, and low-temperature streaks within the near-wall region. Meanwhile, an increase in the Mach number weakens the preferential concentration of particles in this near-wall region, which is associated with the enhanced near-wall coherent structures. Furthermore, the effects of flow compressibility and rarefaction on particle transport promote the concentration of particles with low inertia (St0+=1,5) and high inertia (St0+=100,200). To further understand this phenomenon, the local Stokes number (Stl+) is employed to quantify the particle inertia relative to the local flow in compressible flows.

papers.title: Experimental study on dynamic pressure and temperature regulation of an accumulator in a mechanically pumped two-phase loop
papers.abstract: To address the challenge of dynamic regulation of phase-change pressure in a mechanically pumped two-phase loop system in microgravity, this paper proposes a two-phase thermally controlled accumulator with a longitudinal gradient capillary wick. The stability and responsiveness of the system pressure are investigated. A streamlined, integrated two-phase experimental apparatus is established to systematically analyze the dynamic variations in pressure and thermodynamic behavior at different initial subcooling levels and vapor volume change rates. The results indicate that the accumulator's design can autonomously regulate internal fluid distribution and maintain a relatively stable vapor volume, thereby mitigating pressure oscillations induced by the interchange of working fluid mass. Furthermore, the variations in reservoir saturation temperature are confined to 1.1 °C without active regulation. The influence of subcooling on system pressure variations during phase change is also discussed, indicating that an active control strategy involving external cooling and internal heating for thermoelectric coolers should be implemented. This study provides a qualitative foundation for optimizing the accumulator structure and formulating the active control strategy.

papers.title: Numerical investigation and experiment of a single-valve dual-port piezoelectric pump inspired by cuttlefish jet propulsion
papers.abstract: This work presents a novel single-valve dual-port piezoelectric pump based on the cuttlefish jet propulsion mechanism, aiming to provide an efficient and stable fluid drive solution. The pump combines the cuttlefish jet propulsion principle with an integrated flexible valve design, achieving high airtightness and excellent fluid control capabilities. Experimental results indicate that the pump, driven by 250 Vp-p, reaches a maximum output pressure of 10.22 kPa and a flow rate of 6.82 ml/min, exhibiting remarkable pumping capability. The pump demonstrates good frequency adaptability across various frequencies, with an outstanding output performance, especially in the low-frequency range of 40–60 Hz. Furthermore, the pump effectively pumps different fluids, including water, milk, and oil, demonstrating excellent adaptability to high-viscosity fluids. Tests on the dual-inlet mixing system show that this design achieves stable fluid mixing with a processing speed of 2.16 ml/min. Pneumatic actuator tests validate the pump's potential as a miniaturized power source for pneumatic control systems, with a maximum output pressure of 12.63 kPa and good linearity when driving the actuator.

papers.title: Efficient inverse reconstruction of internal flow fields in rocket engine combustion chambers based on diffusion models
papers.abstract: The internal flow field of a rocket engine combustion chamber is crucial for performance evaluation and design optimization. Traditional numerical simulations suffer from long computation times and low inversion efficiency and are difficult to apply in the real engine design and optimization. This study employed the data-driven reconstruction method for the combustion chamber's internal flow field based on measurable data from the outside. The present study is based on a 490 N attitude and orbit control engine as the test case, and a multi-condition dataset was generated through high-precision simulations. A diffusion model-based neural network was then trained, where measurable data guided the generation process to achieve fast and accurate flow field inversion. The results show that the proposed method achieves an average error of only 2.13% on the validation set, with inversion speed three orders of magnitude faster than conventional simulations. The effects of observation point density and noise intensity were also analyzed: as the number of observation points decreased from 80% to 20%, the average prediction error increased linearly from 2.13% to 4.03%. When the maximum signal-to-noise ratio varied from 40 to 10 dB, the error first decreased to 1.81% and then rose to 3.59%, demonstrating strong robustness against noisy data.

papers.title: Energy-driven mechanism of a flat box girder in bending–torsional coupled flutter
papers.abstract: Various nonlinear aerodynamic force frameworks have been proposed to explain the complicated nonlinear phenomena during bending–torsional coupled flutter. Whereas these frameworks are mainly applicable to their respective situations and lack universality. The present study aims to explore the energy-driven mechanism of a flat box girder in bending–torsional coupled flutter from the fundamental perspective of energy. Experimental investigations on a flat box girder were conducted using the forced vibration method to study nonlinear aerodynamic forces under various coupled motion parameters, such as bending and torsional motion amplitudes, as well as the phase lag between them. Based on energy input and dissipation by aerodynamic forces, the concept of dimensionless aerodynamic work was employed to comprehensively quantify the nonlinear aerodynamic effects on structural energy excitation. Nonlinear energy maps for bending–torsional coupled motion states were constructed, and a comparative analysis of the evolving trends in these maps under different motion parameters was performed. The role of phase lag between bending and torsional motions in regulating aerodynamic energy transferring effects is exploited from the phase lag relationships. The mutual energy input effect of the bending and torsional two-degrees-of-system on the occurrence and development of coupled flutter is clarified by energy maps. Finally, the sophisticated multiple limit cycle oscillation states and corresponding development paths are graphically represented utilizing the energy maps with aerodynamic damping form.

papers.title: Analysis of time-frequency characteristics and the impact of advanced coefficients on electromagnetic wakes generated by rotating propellers
papers.abstract: In the marine environment, the rotation of propellers induces charged ion movement in the wake, generating an electromagnetic field influenced by the ambient geomagnetic field. This electromagnetic signal is crucial for non-acoustic underwater target detection. However, the complex interactions among hydrodynamics, ion motion, and electromagnetic fields in the formation of the propeller's electromagnetic wake have not been systematically explored. To investigate the evolution and time-frequency characteristics of this wake, we developed a theoretical model that integrates propeller wake dynamics, seawater ion movement, and electromagnetic fields through a multiphysics coupling approach. High-fidelity numerical simulations replicated the hydrodynamic and electromagnetic wake evolution induced by propeller rotation. The study provides a comprehensive analysis of the wake's evolution and spatial distribution, with an in-depth examination of frequency domain characteristics at various distances behind the propeller. Additionally, we assessed the impact of the propeller's advance coefficient on the electromagnetic wake. The results indicate that a low advance coefficient amplifies vortex and turbulence effects, leading to greater fluctuations in the induced magnetic field, while a high advance coefficient reduces turbulence, producing a more stable magnetic signal with blade-passing frequency characteristics that persist over longer distances. These findings enhance our understanding of electromagnetic wakes, potentially advancing future efforts in underwater target detection and tracking.

papers.title: Temporal–spatial spray characteristics of self-excited sweeping nozzles in crossflow: An experimental investigation
papers.abstract: Self-excited sweeping (SES) nozzles have attracted growing interest due to their ability to generate high-frequency oscillating jets. While prior studies have clarified their flow dynamics and atomization under atmospheric conditions, their behavior in crossflow—relevant to aero-engine and afterburner combustors—remains insufficiently understood. This study experimentally investigates the spray characteristics of a SES nozzle operating in a high-speed crossflow, with an emphasis on the influence of injection pressure. A two-dimensional phase Doppler particle analyzer (PDPA) was employed to measure droplet size and velocity distributions at multiple downstream locations. The results show that the spray morphology evolves markedly downstream. Droplet sizes decrease significantly up to the midstream region, while axial velocities increase due to momentum exchange with the crossflow. The sweeping motion of the SES nozzle induces a dominant oscillation frequency of spray characteristics. The amplitude of these oscillations varies spatially, reflecting the combined effects of sweeping dynamics and aerodynamic damping. Compared to the circular nozzle, the SES nozzle exhibits distinct spray characteristics. The circular nozzle demonstrates greater penetration, but the SES nozzle provides wider lateral coverage, a larger overall spray area, and smaller droplets. Injection pressure is found to be a critical parameter governing spray penetration, coverage, droplet size, and oscillatory behavior. Increasing pressure enhances penetration but results in a trade-off with spanwise coverage. At higher pressures, stronger atomization reduces both Sauter mean diameter and oscillation amplitudes. Overall, this work provides insights into the temporal–spatial spray characteristics of SES nozzles in crossflow environments, offering guidance for their application in aerospace propulsion systems.

papers.title: Simulation of bubbly flow in non-Newtonian fluids using computational fluid dynamics and population balance model based on the entire turbulent energy spectrum
papers.abstract: To investigate the effects of interfacial force models and the coalescence and breakup models for bubbly flow simulation in non-Newtonian fluids, visualization experiments were conducted in a rectangle bubble column. Particle image velocimetry and shadowgraphy were employed to measure bubbly flow in shear-thinning fluids. By extending the kernel functions to the entire turbulent energy spectrum, the simulation accurately captured bubble coalescence and breakup behaviors, leading to improved predictions of bubble size distribution. The results indicate that the Liao and Lehr models underestimated bubble coalescence frequency, while the Luo model overestimated it. The Prince–Blanch model provided the most accurate description of bubble size and distribution. The primary mechanisms driving bubble coalescence in the system were identified as buoyancy-driven motion, wake entrainment, and viscous shear. A comparison of drag force models developed for non-Newtonian fluids in previous literature revealed that, at low superficial gas velocities, the differences in predicted velocity fields and bubble sizes among various drag models were minimal. However, the HosenB and Li models predicted larger liquid velocity. As the superficial gas velocity increased, these discrepancies became more pronounced, with all models except HosenB underestimating the velocity. Additionally, other interfacial forces, including lift force, turbulent dispersion force, and wall lubrication force, were compared, revealing that lift force and turbulent dispersion force significantly influenced the simulation outcomes.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic properties of bubbles of different scales in a gas–liquid–solid system
papers.abstract: Understanding the properties of bubbles and their impact on flow dynamics is essential in systems involving gas, liquid, and solid phases. This research introduces a groundbreaking theoretical analysis of the hydrodynamic behaviors and interactions of bubbles across different scales.
